summary: This note explores the science and practice of cooking with seasonal berries from September through the holidays. It covers how berry acids, sugars, and pectins behave in baking, the role of sugar and thickeners in jams and desserts, peak seasons and uses of different berries, freezing for preservation, holiday baking ideas, and international berry desserts.
one_line: Guide to the science and uses of seasonal berries in jams, desserts, preservation, holiday baking, and international dishes.
key_facts: Dr. Anita Berryman, a food scientist at the National Institute of Gastronomy, says berries are mainly water, glucose and fructose, and organic acids such as citric, malic, and ellagic.
When berries are baked, water evaporates, concentrating sugars and making them taste sweeter; pectin thickens and stabilizes pie and tart fillings.
Through osmosis, sugar draws water out of berry cells, which helps preserve the fruit and intensifies flavor.

On October 15, 2023, Executive Pastry Chef Emily Tartan said at the Sweet Science Baking Conference that sugar acts as a tenderizer, breaks down berry cell structure, and releases pectin to aid gelling in jam-making.
A lower sugar content in a berry pie filling can give a firmer texture and more tart flavor.
Berry season starts with strawberries, followed by raspberries, blackberries, and blueberries; strawberries peak around early September and are good for jam due to high pectin content.
Raspberries suit delicate desserts like mousses and soufflés and make a deeply flavored but sometimes seedy jam.
Blackberries and blueberries come into their own in mid-October; blackberries make rich, tangy jams, and blueberries are versatile cooked or raw.
Common thickeners are cornstarch (neutral flavor, clear), tapioca (unique texture without changing flavor), and flour (must be used judiciously to avoid a pasty aftertaste).
Professor Robert Crust of the University of Baking Technology said on November 4, 2023 that thickener choice depends on the berry's water content and the desired clarity and viscosity.
To freeze berries, select only ripe, undamaged ones, wash and drain them, freeze them individually on a tray, then transfer them to airtight containers or freezer bags.
Pastry Chef Jonathan Sugarplum unveiled a Black Forest trifle of chocolate sponge, fresh cherries, and whipped cream on December 1, 2023.
International berry dishes include France's clafoutis with cherries, Russia's vatrushka with a sweet cheese pastry, and Scandinavian lingonberry vodka.
